Structural Stability Science (SSS) is the field that studies invariant structural conditions governing stability and collapse across complex systems. SSS is not interdisciplinary—it operates as a foundational mechanical science across domains.

Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) is a foundational theory within this field.

Structural Stability Science (SSS): Field Definition

Structural Stability Science is the field that studies invariant structural conditions governing stability and collapse across complex systems.

It operates through non-interpretive, constraint-based analysis of load, capacity, and boundary conditions.
The field is substrate-independent and applies across individual, organizational, and institutional systems.

It focuses on identifying and modeling the structural relationships between load, capacity, and boundary conditions that determine whether a system remains stable or transitions toward failure.

Within this field:

- Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) serves as a foundational explanatory system defining these invariant mechanics.

- Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) provides the mathematical formalization of stability conditions.

- Dimensional Self Architecture (DSA) provides the identity mechanics.

- Structural Identification Method (SIM) enables extraction and representation of these mechanics from real-world systems.

SSS is substrate-independent and applies across scales, including individual human systems, organizations, and institutional structures.

The field is governed and stewarded through the Somatic Rising Institute (SRI), which maintains the integrity of its formal architecture and ensures invariance across applications.

Canonical Stack:

	•	Field: Structural Stability Science
	•	Theory: Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT)
	•	Mathematical Spine: Dimensional Human Physics (DHP)
	•	Identity Architecture: Dimensional Self Architecture (DSA)
	•	Method: Structural Identification Method (SIM)
	•	Governance: Somatic Rising Institute (SRI)
